sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Build settings and security headers
sections.what: Sets how the app is built and installed, and attaches security headers to every page. Also tells browsers not to cache the service worker file.
sections.why: Headers protect users from framing attacks, insecure connections, and some script injection. Not caching the service worker lets updates arrive.
sections.watch_out: The connect rule lists a staging address, so check it before each release so production API calls are not blocked.

summary: Tells the hosting service how to build the web app and sets the security headers sent with every page.
purpose: Controls the build and deployment, and adds protections such as blocking framing, requiring HTTPS, and limiting which sites scripts and data can load from.
why: Security headers protect users from common web attacks. The file header is not visible, so the exact reason is not stated in the code.
how: Sets the framework, build command, and install command. Then attaches a list of security headers to every page, and sets no caching for the service worker file.
inputs: The project code, the build commands, and the hosting platform's settings.
outputs: The built web app, with the listed headers sent in each response.
risks: The content security policy allows inline and eval scripts, which weakens protection against injected code. The connect rule lists a staging API address, so production API calls may be blocked unless that address is updated. Some headers, such as the old XSS protection header, have little effect in modern browsers.
debug: If API calls fail in production with a policy error in the browser console, check the connect rule and the live API address. If the page does not load a font or image, check the matching rule. If the build fails, check the build and install commands.
